overview: Memeware 7.3's Speed is an eight-mode movement module built on three event consumers: a PacketInEvent handler that watches for S08PacketPlayerPosLook teleports and disables the module with a chat message when Flag Check is on, a MovementEvent handler that dispatches the per-server modes and rewrites the movement delta, and an UpdateEvent pre handler that records lastDistance from the position history for the air-decay math. The modes span a brute-force Vanilla pin (0.47 blocks per tick), friction-styled NCP hops via DynamicFriction, a block-placement Mineplex2, spectate-packet Cubecraft modes, and a Hypixel bhop that runs a 1.25 timer on ground contact.

sections.p: Module state is three fields (speed, currentDistance, lastDistance, plus the prevOnGround flag) and one DynamicFriction instance. The PacketInEvent consumer cancels nothing - it is a tripwire: any S08 teleport while Flag Check is on prints a chat message and toggles the module off, so the user is warned the mode flagged instead of being left to accumulate violations. The MovementEvent consumer is the mode dispatcher; every branch ends by writing the event delta through MovementUtils.setMoveSpeed(event, speed), which recomputes the x/z from the yaw and the WASD state. onEnable resets speed, prevOnGround and lastDistance; onDisable restores timerSpeed 1.0, zeroes jumpMovementFactor and the motion fields, and for the Cubecraft modes resets motionY and nudges the player up 0.2664 blocks to clear the block-placement residue.

Vanilla is a straight pin: setMoveSpeed(event, 0.47) every tick with no hop at all. PvPTemple hops with a 0.42 jump, pins 0.5 on the ground tick, boosts to 0.8 on the first air tick, then decays by 0.932 per tick. Mineplex jumps with 0.4, captures the current speed into currentDistance on the ground tick and resets speed to 0, then on the first air tick sets speed = currentDistance + 0.56 and afterwards multiplies lastDistance (measured in the UpdateEvent pre handler from the previous-position delta) by 0.985, 0.98 or 0.975 depending on magnitude, clamped to a 0.42 floor. Hypixel runs the timer at 1.25 on ground ticks with a 0.3999175222222555 jump and speed = baseMoveSpeed * 2.1492287832, then bleeds 0.66333332222 * (speed - base) on the first air tick and decays by speed/160 - 1.0E-9 afterwards, with a 1.73E-11 Y nudge in the pre update to keep the server's move window open. Cubecraft Slow sends a C18 spectate packet for the CubeUtil UUID every tick, suppresses the jump key, and pulses the speed between base + 1.276444466666 every 4th tick and base + 1.0E-12 otherwise; Cubecraft Fast pulses base + 1.55522225, teleports Y up by 0.0922 * rand(0.75, 1) on every 4th ground tick, and offsets XZ by 0.12115522522 every 8th tick. NCP Fast delegates to DynamicFriction.updateFriction with a 0.3929 hop, speed = max(base * 1.14999, speed * 1.14999) on the ground, a first-air bleed of 0.66 * (speed - base), and a speed/159 decay - the classic NCP hop that holds speed just above the base value. Mineplex2 swaps the held item to an empty hotbar slot (C09) and places a block under the player every 3rd ground tick, adding 0.125 to speed up to a 1.24 cap and decaying by 0.98 otherwise.

All modes route through MovementUtils.setMoveSpeed(event, moveSpeed). The helper normalizes forward/strafe to -1/0/1, blends diagonals with the sin/cos of 0.6398355709958845, and for the event variant applies the 45-degree yaw offsets (-45 when strafing right while moving forward, +45 when strafing left, 90 for pure strafe) before writing event.setX/setZ; the motion-variant writes motionX/motionZ directly. getBaseMoveSpeed returns 0.2873 scaled by 1 + 0.2 * (amplifier + 1) per speed-potion level, which the Hypixel and Cubecraft modes multiply against. The S08 tripwire is the module's only anti-flag mechanism: it does not spoof onGround, does not cancel packets, and does not adjust the timer except in the Hypixel and Mineplex modes, so each mode is defined almost entirely by its horizontal speed schedule and its hop height.

files.label: Speed.java (module)
files.explanation: The module is three event consumers. eventConsumer0 (PacketInEvent) is the flag tripwire: on any S08PacketPlayerPosLook with Flag Check enabled it prints a chat message and toggles the module off, which is the only protection the module has against teleport-based rollbacks. eventConsumer1 (MovementEvent) is the mode machine - every mode branch computes a speed value and ends in MovementUtils.setMoveSpeed(event, speed) so the reported delta is exactly the module's vector. eventConsumer2 (UpdateEvent) runs in the pre phase: it records lastDistance from hypot(posX - prevPosX, posZ - prevPosZ), which the Mineplex mode multiplies against for its air decay. The Mineplex2 branch is the only one that sends packets of its own: C09 held-item changes to an empty slot and back, around BlockUtil.placeHeldItemUnderPlayer, building speed from block placement every third ground tick. onDisable restores the timer and motion and, for Cubecraft modes, lifts the player 0.2664 blocks to compensate the block-placement Y drift.

files.label: MovementUtils.java (strafe math)
files.explanation: MovementUtils is the single helper every mode calls. setMoveSpeed(MovementEvent, double) is the event variant used by the module: it normalizes the input state, applies the 45/90-degree yaw offsets for diagonal and pure-strafe movement, and writes the event x/z so the packet the server validates matches the vector the mode intended. The motion variant setMoveSpeed(double) writes motionX/motionZ directly and is what the Fly module reuses. getDirection() mirrors the yaw math (180-degree flip when backing, 90 * forward per strafe key) and is used by offsetXZ, which teleports the player along the movement heading - the Cubecraft Fast XZ offset. getBaseMoveSpeed returns 0.2873 scaled by speed potions, the anchor for every multiplier in the Hypixel and Cubecraft modes. The same file carries fallPacket() and ascendPacket(), the 8-block C04 ladders that Nekoware's Fly Anti-Kick uses, so the utility is shared across the movement family.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (horizontal speed envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly rebuilds the client's physics from the world and compares the reported move against it. prepareSpeedEstimation picks inertia and acceleration by medium (on-ground friction cubed, air acceleration) and estimateNextSpeed predicts the per-tick distance; the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back, and the ground state comes from a block ray trace rather than the packet flag. Every Memeware mode lands above the ~0.28-0.31 sprint prediction: Vanilla's 0.47 pin produces an offset of about 0.16 (violation ~16 on the first move), PvPTemple's 0.8 air tick is worse, Mineplex's +0.56 air boost and Cubecraft's +1.28 to +1.56 over base are far beyond the envelope, and Hypixel's 2.149x base (0.617) breaches it on the first hop. Only the vertical side is protected: the 0.4-0.42 jumps match the vanilla jump envelope and NCP grants a 10-tick jumpDelay for immediate re-jumps, so the hdistrel tag is the only signal - and it is a set-back every time.

countering.label: Speed (BunnyHop / onGround expected)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Speed builds expected = 0.2873 + stage per move, where the air stage is 0.049 at zero vertical, 0.08 descending below 0.34, and 0.3261 while rising. Vanilla's 0.47 pin, PvPTemple's 0.8 air boost, Mineplex's +0.56 first-air tick, Cubecraft Slow's 1.2764 pulse and Cubecraft Fast's 1.5552 pulse all exceed the descending expectation of 0.3673 and flag the BunnyHop offground_expected branch with measured and expected values in the message; Hypixel's 0.617 exceeds even the rising expectation of 0.6134 on the way up and the 0.3673 expectation on the way down. The one mode that mostly stays under the air stages is NCP Fast, whose DynamicFriction decay holds the speed just above the base value (~0.331-0.36) - but its ground ticks re-pin at base * 1.14999, and the ground branch (expected = thisMove / groundTime + baseMove, active after 5+ grounded ticks) catches it whenever the player runs on the surface without hopping. Non-failing moves store the from location as the set-back.

countering.label: Speed (momentum model, discrepancy accumulator)
countering.explanation: Hawk's Speed predicts expected = friction * lastSpeed * handleMultipliers + (maxForce + handleAdders + EPSILON) and accumulates the difference as a Discrepancy; when the total passes 0.1 the check punishes with VL = discrepancy * 10 and rubber-bands to the server position. The Vanilla pin is the cleanest failure: with ground friction 0.6 and lastSpeed pinned at 0.47, expected lands near 0.33, so the first jump tick alone contributes a discrepancy around 0.14 - over the threshold immediately. PvPTemple and Mineplex are worse because their air boosts (0.8 and +0.56) make the discrepancy grow on the first air tick, and Hypixel's 2.149x multiplier produces a mismatch of several tenths per hop. The jump and step exemptions only forgive the vanilla sprint-jump adder, so none of the modes can claim them: the pinned magnitudes are simply not explainable by momentum conservation.
